question.value: How prevalent is acetamide (CH3CONH2) across hot molecular cores in high-mass star-forming regions, and how do its abundance and formation pathways relate to formamide (NH2CHO)?

evidence.quote: We present the first systematic survey for acetamide toward 52 hot molecular cores using ALMA Band 6 data.
Our detections substantially increase the number of known acetamide sources, enabling a comparative analysis with formamide.
This work makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.00095.S.
QUARKS is a 1.3 mm follow-up to the ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-forming Regions (cite: Liu20)
The QUARKS survey was conducted with ACA and 12 m arrays at Band 6 towards 139 protoclusters from October 2021 to June 2024.

claims.hypothesis: Acetamide (CH3CONH2) is more widespread in high-mass star-forming hot molecular cores than previously recognized from sparse individual detections.
claims.experiment: Conducted a systematic line survey toward 52 hot molecular cores using ALMA Band 6 data from the QUARKS survey, requiring at least five unblended transitions with S/N >= 3sigma matching LTE synthetic spectra.
claims.result: Confidently detected CH3CONH2 (along with NH2CHO and NH2^13CHO) in 10 HMCs, with column densities from (2.5+-0.9)e14 to (1.5+-0.6)e16 cm^-2, increasing the total number of known CH3CONH2 sources to 17.
claims.finding: Complex amides such as acetamide are more prevalent in high-mass star-forming regions than previously thought.

evidence.quote: Acetamide has been detected in 10 cores, markedly expanding the inventory of known emitters.
Both NH$_{2}$CHO and CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ were detected in ten HMCs, increasing the number of known CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ sources to 17 and providing the most extensive sample to date for this molecule.

claims.hypothesis: Acetamide (CH3CONH2) and formamide (NH2CHO) share a chemically linked formation pathway dominated by grain-surface reactions followed by thermal co-desorption.
claims.experiment: Derived column densities and CH3OH-normalized abundances of CH3CONH2 and NH2CHO across the 10 detected HMCs, mapped their spatial distributions, fitted their abundance correlation across diverse sources, and compared abundance ratios with gas-phase and grain-surface astrochemical models and laboratory ice experiments.
claims.result: Found similar compact spatial distributions, a strong power-law correlation X(CH3CONH2) = (0.08+-0.07) X(NH2CHO)^(0.86+-0.15), and a nearly constant NH2CHO/CH3CONH2 ratio ranging from 2.9 to 8.9 (mean 5.6+-1.8), matching Garrod et al. (2022) grain-surface model predictions (5-13) and laboratory ice desorption ratios (~2.5).
claims.finding: CH3CONH2 and NH2CHO are chemically linked and predominantly synthesized via grain-surface chemistry (involving the NH2CO intermediate) followed by thermal co-desorption.

evidence.loc: Chemical links between NH2CHO and CH3CONH2
evidence.quote: The NH$_{2}$CHO/CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ ratios in our sample range from 2.9 to 8.9, with an average of $\sim$5.6 and a standard deviation of $\pm$1.8, exhibiting relatively small variation across sources (Fig. [4](#fig:fig. 4)b).
Our observed abundance ratios (2.9–8.9) align with Garrod et al.’s predicted range (5–13), providing strong support for a linked formation pathway through grain-surface chemistry.

Taken together, these findings strongly favor a formation scenario in which CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ is synthesized via grain-surface chemistry closely linked to NH$_{2}$CHO, followed by co-desorption in star-forming regions.

claims.hypothesis: High CH3OH column density is a sufficient predictor for detecting CH3CONH2 in hot molecular cores.
claims.experiment: Derived 3sigma column density upper limits for CH3CONH2 in the 42 non-detected HMCs and compared CH3CONH2/CH3OH ratios against CH3OH column densities across the full sample of 52 HMCs.
claims.result: All 10 CH3CONH2 detections occur in sources with higher CH3OH column densities, but 6 non-detected sources with CH3OH column densities > 4e18 cm^-2 show no CH3CONH2 detection.
claims.finding: CH3CONH2 is more likely to be detected in chemically rich environments, but high CH3OH abundance alone is not a sufficient predictor for CH3CONH2 detection.

evidence.loc: The upper limits of column density for CH3CONH2 in undetected sources.
evidence.quote: All ten CH$_3$CONH$_2$-detected sources exhibit higher CH$_3$OH column densities, supporting the idea that CH$_3$CONH$_2$ is more likely to be detected in chemically rich environments.

evidence.loc: The upper limits of column density for CH3CONH2 in undetected sources.
evidence.quote: Nonetheless, 6 non-detected sources with CH$_3$OH column densities \> $4\times10^{18} {\rm cm^{-2}}$, show no CH$_3$CONH$_2$ detection, suggesting that CH$_3$OH abundance alone is not a sufficient predictor.

why_this_data.value: Selected 52 HMC candidates from the ALMA Band 6 QUARKS survey, which resolves substructures within 3 mm core clusters at ~1.3 arcsec resolution with four 1.875 GHz spectral windows at 1.2 km s^-1 velocity resolution, sufficient to resolve broad molecular lines and conduct the first systematic search for acetamide.

evidence.quote: To address this gap, we present the first systematic search for acetamide across 52 hot molecular cores (HMCs) using Band 6 observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).
The uniform spectral resolution of 976.56 kHz corresponds to a velocity resolution ($\delta$$V$) of 1.2 km s$^{-1}$, sufficient to spectrally resolve broad molecular lines.

why_this_method.value: Extracted spectra at offset positions to avoid continuum absorption and severe line blending at continuum peaks; used optically thin NH2^13CHO scaled by 12C/13C ratios because main NH2CHO lines are optically thick; normalized abundances to CH3OH instead of H2 due to uncertainties in dust opacity.

evidence.quote: To improve line identification in such cases, spectra were extracted from offset positions (as shown in Fig. [6](#fig:fig. A1) in the Appendix), where most of the lines exhibit Gaussian profiles and are relatively bright compared to other positions.

Due to optical thickness of NH$_{2}$CHO lines, their column densities were instead derived from the optically thin NH$_{2}$$^{13}$CHO isotopolog, scaled by the appropriate $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio for each source.
Abundances relative to H$_{2}$ are not reported due to uncertainties in dust opacity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gas-phase formation routes for CH3CONH2 (addition of CH2 radical to NH2CHO, or radiative association between NH2CHO and CH3+), rejected due to high energy barriers (>1000 K for CH2 spin-flip) or predicted abundances (~10^-15) far below observed levels.

evidence.quote: However, theoretical studies by (cite: Qua07) indicate that this reaction requires a spin-flip transition of CH$_{2}$ from the triplet to singlet state, with an energy barrier exceeding 1000 K—rendering it unlikely under typical interstellar conditions.

Other proposed gas-phase reactions, such as radiative association between NH$_{2}$CHO and CH$^{+}_{3}$ (cite: Qua07), predict CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ abundances ($\sim$10$^{-15}$) far below observed levels.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extracting spectra at the continuum peak, rejected in favor of offset positions because of severe line blending and strong NH2CHO absorption against bright continuum emission at the center.

evidence.quote: A detailed line-by-line inspection revealed that most CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ transitions are blended with other species near the continuum peak, while NH$_{2}$CHO transitions suffer from significant absorption against bright continuum emission.

To improve line identification in such cases, spectra were extracted from offset positions (as shown in Fig. [6](#fig:fig. A1) in the Appendix), where most of the lines exhibit Gaussian profiles and are relatively bright compared to other positions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rotational diagram fitting for CH3CONH2 in I18089, rejected because the five detected transitions span a narrow upper-level energy range (117.7-136.6 K).

evidence.quote: For CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ in I18089, the rotational diagram was not employed due to the limited energy range (117.7-136.6 K) of five detected transitions, which precludes a reliable fit.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Required at least five unblended transitions with S/N >= 3sigma matching modeled rest frequencies and intensities for a confident detection of CH3CONH2, and at least three unblended transitions spanning a broad energy range to apply rotational diagram fitting.

evidence.quote: CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ was considered confidently detected in ten HMCs (see Table [\[table:table 2\]](#table:table 2)), each showing at least five unblended transitions with signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) $\geq$ 3$\sigma$ that match the modeled rest frequencies and intensities.
Column densities and excitation temperatures were derived using rotational diagrams for molecules with at least three unblended transitions spanning a broad energy range (Fig. [2](#fig:fig. 2)).

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties in the adopted 12C/13C ratios from distance effects, beam size variations, excitation temperature mismatches, isotope-selective photodissociation, and chemical fractionation.

evidence.quote: While this method effectively avoids opacity-related biases, several factors may introduce uncertainties into the observed $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios.
As noted by (cite: Yan23), these include distance effects, beam size variations, excitation temperature mismatches, isotope-selective photodissociation, and chemical fractionation.

limitations_admitted.value: Abundances relative to H2 cannot be reported due to uncertainties in dust opacity.

evidence.quote: Abundances relative to H$_{2}$ are not reported due to uncertainties in dust opacity.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties in excitation temperatures, optical depth, line blending, spatial structure, LTE assumptions, use of 13C isotopologs for NH2CHO, and uniform source-filling assumption for CH3CONH2 may introduce systematic uncertainties in derived column densities and ratios.

evidence.loc: Chemical links between NH2CHO and CH3CONH2
evidence.quote: While uncertainties in excitation temperatures significantly affect the derived column densities, other contributors include optical depth, line blending, spatial structure, and assumptions of LTE.

evidence.loc: Chemical links between NH2CHO and CH3CONH2
evidence.quote: Additionally, the adopted assumption of uniform source-filling emission for CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ may lead to systematic uncertainties.

referee_caveats_inferred: The exact R.A./Dec. coordinates of the offset spectral extraction positions (shown only visually in Fig. A1) are not tabulated, yet column densities at hot core edges can vary strongly with small positional shifts (as seen in the comparison of I17175 MM1/MM2 with Ligterink et al. 2020).

CH3OH column densities from Qin et al. (2022) were used to normalize the amide column densities, but it is not explicitly stated whether the CH3OH column densities were re-extracted at the exact same offset positions used for the amides in this paper.
For 9 of the 10 sources, NH2^13CHO column densities were computed assuming the rotational temperature of CH3CONH2 rather than an independently measured NH2^13CHO temperature.

data_public_as_stated.value: Derived data and Tables C.1-C.10 are publicly available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16673390); ALMA project code ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.00095.S is stated.

evidence.quote: The derived data underlying this article are available in the article and in its online supplementary material on [zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16673390).
This work makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.00095.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Exact celestial coordinates (R.A. and Dec.) of the offset extraction pixels for each of the 10 detected HMCs
Imaging and array-combination scripts/parameters (ACA + 12m TM2 combination weights, tclean robust parameter, continuum subtraction channels) deferred to Liu et al. (2024)
Specific unblended transitions and velocity integration windows used for the moment-0 maps in Figure 3
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several hundred GB to ~1-2 TB for the combined ACA + 12m Band 6 spectral cubes across 52 hot molecular cores (4 SPWs of 1920 channels each), or a few MB for the extracted 1D spectra and Zenodo tables.
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project code is stated, line tables and derived data are hosted on Zenodo, and the LTE rotational diagram methodology and equations are clearly specified. However, full end-to-end reproduction from raw data requires imaging details from Liu et al. (2024) and the exact coordinates of the offset spectral extraction positions, which are only plotted visually in Figure A1.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2021.1.00095.S) and supplementary line tables (Zenodo) are public, and the main results are concrete numeric column densities, excitation temperatures, and abundance ratios derived via standard LTE rotational diagrams.

methods_papers.why: Standard rotational diagram formalism used for LTE column density and excitation temperature calculations
Galactocentric distance relation used to calculate 12C/13C isotope ratios for scaling NH2^13CHO to NH2CHO

companion_papers.why: ALMA-QUARKS survey overview paper providing systemic velocities, observational setup, and data reduction details
ATOMS survey paper identifying the 52 HMC candidates and providing the reference CH3OH column densities
ATOMS 3 mm survey paper providing the Galactocentric distances of the target clumps

related_projects_or_surveys: ALMA-QUARKS (Querying Underlying mechanisms of massive star formation with ALMA-Resolved gas Kinematics and Structures)
ATOMS (ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-forming Regions)
